sentences.text: Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned Senior Advocate along  Yogesh Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Kamal Kumar Tiwari, learned Govt. Advocate for t  respondent/State.
ORDER Heard and perused the case diary.

2] This is the applicant's first application under section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023.

The applicant is implicated in connection with Crime No.148/2024 registered at Police Station M.G. Road, District-Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471,
474, 120-B, 409 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The applicant is lodged in jail since 01.06.2024.

3] The allegation against the applicant is that he was also involved in the aforesaid case wherein,
huge amount was defrauded by the accused persons in the Municipal Corporation, Indore by submitting forged bills.
4] Learned Senior counsel appearing for the applicant has submitted NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:3267 2 MCRC-472-2025 that admittedly, the applicant has not received any amount in his account.
So far as the order of trial Court dated 24.10.2024 is concerned, certainly it has been mentioned that disputed signature was similar to the present applicant's signature.

sentences.text: 1 of hand writing expert has been received but nothing is found against the applicant.

Since nothing has been seized from the present applicant in this particular crime number, he is entitled for grant of bail likewise, other persons who have been released on bail because they have not received any amount.
There is no other material available to connect the applicant with the offence.
It is further submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 01.06.2024, and the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take a long time.
Thus, it is submitted that the application may be allowed.
5] Counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that there is nothing against the present applicant in hand writing expert report.
He has also submitted that the applicant has not received any amount in this particular crime number.

However,
he has also submitted that the applicant received amount in Crime No. 134/2024 and in Crime No.
190/2024 received amount of Rs.1,09,80,000/-.
Therefore, bail should not be allowed.

6] On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the case- diary as also taking note of the fact that applicant has not received any amount in this particular crime number and on the similar grounds, he has been granted bail vide order dated 17.12.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 50703/2024 by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, this Court is inclined to allow the present bail application.
Accordingly, without commenting on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3267 3 MCRC-472-2025 merits of the case, the present application is allowed.

7] The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 480 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

8] This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified Copy as per rules.
